vignette_preview:
A 4-year-old boy presented with a 3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions. Previous treatments with various topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement. His mother reported occasional otitis media. The family history was negative for skin disease.

Multiple disseminated erythematous papules, petechial hemorrhages, and yellowish crusts were present on the scalp. The remaining skin and mucosal surfaces were unremarkable. Neck, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes showed no abnormalities. No other obvious physical abnormalities were noted.

- Laboratory tests: Routine blood examinations revealed no pathological findings.- Imaging studies:  Title: Whole-body MRI  Description: Two osteolytic lesions identified on the right frontoparietal skull  - Pathological examination:  Title: Punch biopsy of scalp (H&E stain)  Description: Subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, solitary lymphocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes    Title: Immunohistochemical staining  Description: The infiltrate stained positively for CD1AAdditional tests:- Ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes: normal- Serum electrophoresis: normal
